question: After the no-op pacing defect is fixed, should outbound recovery keep ambiguous entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed?
rationale: Both states are defensible: pending preserves future recoverability, while failed gives operators a clearer terminal state; tests cannot choose that product and operations tradeoff.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
options.body: Merge after the pacing fix and green validation if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous rows to stay recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the broader delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a doctor, UI, or API surface before changing ambiguous rows to remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
recommendation.body: Merge after the pacing fix and green validation if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous rows to stay recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses SQLite queue state semantics, operator behavior, and the broader delivery consistency design.
